title: Currying a pair of sheaf evaluations
statement: Let $C$ be a category with objects in universe $u$ and morphisms in universe $v$, let $J$ be a Grothendieck topology on $C$, and let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings in universe $\max(u,v)$. Let $S,A,H,B,D$ be sheaves of $R$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and let $f:S\to\mathcal Hom_R(A,H)$ and $g:H\to\mathcal Hom_R(B,D)$ be sheaf morphisms, with internal Hom as in [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Put $\tau_{A,B}:A\otimes_{p,R}B\to (A\otimes_R B)_{\mathrm{pre}}$ for the module-sheafification unit followed by the inverse of the tensor comparison [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. There exists $b:S\to\mathcal Hom_R(A\otimes_R B,D)$ such that for every $U\in C$, $s\in S(U)$, object $(W\to U)$ of $C/U$, $x\in A(W)$ and $y\in B(W)$, one has $b_U(s)_W(\tau_{A,B,W}(x\otimes y))=g_W(f_U(s)_W(x))_{(W\xrightarrow{1}W)}(y)$. Here a section of internal Hom over an object is a morphism on its slice site, so both displayed evaluations use the indicated slice objects. No complexes, product families, coproducts, uniqueness or invertibility are asserted.

proof.text: Uncurry f and g on the underlying presheaves by the sectionwise balanced tensor universal property. Braiding and associativity give the restriction-compatible trilinear map s tensor (x tensor y) mapped to g(f(s)(x))(y). Curry the S input to obtain A.val tensor B.val -> internalHom(S,D). All constructions are actual presheaf morphisms with sectionwise linear maps; their naturality is checked on pure tensors.

Since internalHom(S,D) is a sheaf, extend the preceding presheaf tensor morphism through the module sheafification adjunction and the tensor comparison, obtaining k:A tensor B -> internalHom(S,D). Its composite with the sheafification unit is the prescribed presheaf map by the adjunction inverse law and the tensor comparison inverse law.

Transpose k by the local pairing: b_U(s) at W takes z to k_W(z) evaluated at the identity slice object and the restriction of s to W. Naturality of this pairing proves that b is a sheaf morphism. On the unit image of x tensor y the preceding factorization reduces to g(f_W(s|W)(x))(y). Naturality of f, evaluated at the identity slice object, identifies f_W(s|W)(x) with f_U(s)_W(x), proving the equation. The same linear constructions handle zero modules, zero rings and empty sites.

theorem homTensorPair_construct (S A H B D : Mod)
    (f : S ⟶ homObj (R := R) A H) (g : H ⟶ homObj (R := R) B D) :
    let := monoidalCategory R
    ∃ b : S ⟶ homObj (R := R) (A ⊗ B) D,
      ∀ (U : Cᵒᵖ) (s : S.val.obj U) (W : (Over U.unop)ᵒᵖ)
        (x : A.val.obj (op W.unop.left)) (y : B.val.obj (op W.unop.left)),
        (((b.val.app U).hom s).app W).hom
          (((PresheafOfModules.sheafificationAdjunction
            (𝟙 ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj R).obj)).unit.app
              (A.val ⊗ B.val) ≫ (tensorObjIsoSheafification (R := R) A B).inv.val).app
                (op W.unop.left) |>.hom (x ⊗ₜ[R.obj.obj (op W.unop.left)] y)) =
        ((((g.val.app (op W.unop.left)).hom
          ((((f.val.app U).hom s).app W).hom x)).app
            (op (Over.mk (𝟙 W.unop.left)))).hom y)
